payload.text: axum middleware footgun for nested services: `Router::new().merge(protected).merge(public).layer(...)` applies the layer ONLY to routes present at `.layer(...)` time. Subsequent `.nest("/mcp", inner)` calls on the result do NOT pick up that layer. Either (a) attach the layer to `inner` before nesting, or (b) `.nest(...).layer(...)` again. klams sprint 007 hit this: `/mcp` was unauthenticated in production because `require_bearer` was layered on the REST sub-router and the MCP nest came later. Fix in `crates/klams-service/src/main.rs`: build `mcp_router = klams_mcp::router(...).layer(from_fn_with_state(auth_state, require_bearer))` then nest. Regression test in `crates/klams-service/tests/mcp_auth.rs`.

rmcp `StreamableHttpServerConfig.allowed_hosts` is a DNS-rebinding Host-header allowlist with a footgun default: when non-empty and the inbound `Host:` header doesn't match, rmcp returns `403 Forbidden: Host header is not allowed` BEFORE any outer middleware (including auth) runs. The previous klams default `["localhost","127.0.0.1","0.0.0.0"]` blocked every operator connecting via a real hostname (e.g. `kubs0:7777`) and confused VS Code's MCP client into a retry-with-new-auth-registration loop. Fix: pass an empty Vec to disable the check, OR drive the allowlist from operator config. klams ships it as `[server].mcp_allowed_hosts` (default empty = disabled, `require_bearer` is the real gate). See `crates/klams-mcp/src/transport.rs` and `crates/klams-service/src/config.rs::ServerConfig`.

VS Code Insiders `"type": "http"` MCP client accepts static bearer auth out of the box via `headers.Authorization` in `.vscode/mcp.json` — no OAuth dance required. Example: `{"klams":{"type":"http","url":"http://host:7777/mcp","headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer <token>"}}}`. Missing `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` endpoints produce two harmless `[warning] Could not fetch resource metadata` lines in the "MCP: <name>" Output panel and then the client proceeds. No "User did not provide client details" / token-paste dialog appears. Verified 2026-05-25 against VS Code Insiders + rmcp 1.7 StreamableHttpService.

Pattern for accessing axum request extensions from inside an rmcp 1.7 `ServerHandler` (e.g. to scope-filter `tools/list` by the caller's auth): rmcp's `StreamableHttpService` injects `http::request::Parts` into the rmcp `RequestContext.extensions`. Pull your own extension out via `ctx.extensions.get::<axum::http::request::Parts>().and_then(|p| p.extensions.get::<MyExt>())`. Documented in rmcp's `tower.rs` doc-comment near `pub struct StreamableHttpService`. klams uses this in `crates/klams-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs::caller_scopes` to enforce FR-020 per-tool scope filtering.

Testing rmcp Streamable HTTP from raw reqwest requires handling: (1) full handshake order — POST `initialize` → capture `mcp-session-id` response header → POST `notifications/initialized` (no id) → then POST `tools/list` etc., all with `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`; (2) when `StreamableHttpServerConfig.json_response = false` (klams default), responses arrive as SSE with `data: <json>

` framing AND interleaved empty `data:
` keep-alive pings — parser must skip empties and take the first `data:` line that successfully parses as JSON. Working harness: `crates/klams-service/tests/mcp_auth.rs::list_tools_with` + `parse_sse_json`. Flip `json_response = true` if you want plain JSON responses (eliminates the `Failed to parse message: ""` warnings VS Code logs on keep-alives).

LVGL swipe-vs-tap disambiguation (kdeskdash, C/LVGL v9 touch dashboard): a swipe that begins on a clickable widget still releases over it, so LVGL fires LV_EVENT_CLICKED even though the user meant to swipe. In every CLICKED callback on a swipe-navigated screen, bail when a gesture is in progress AND NULL-guard the indev: `lv_indev_t *indev = lv_indev_active(); if (indev && lv_indev_get_gesture_dir(indev) != LV_DIR_NONE) return;`. Two gotchas: (1) lv_indev_get_gesture_dir() dereferences its arg with NO NULL check (lib/lvgl/src/indev/lv_indev.c) and lv_indev_active() can return NULL for programmatically dispatched events — so `lv_indev_get_gesture_dir(lv_indev_active())` is a latent NULL deref; a GoL ce-review caught 3 button callbacks doing exactly this. (2) The widget consumes the gesture by default — add LV_OBJ_FLAG_GESTURE_BUBBLE to the panel + every button + label so the swipe still reaches the shell's screen-level LV_EVENT_GESTURE navigation. For region-sensitive taps, capture the press point on LV_EVENT_PRESSED (gesture not yet classified at press time) and decide on LV_EVENT_CLICKED. Plain helpers called from a guarded callback need no guard. Pattern bit twice: src/modes/menu.c tile_cb (canonical, commented) then src/modes/game_of_life.c canvas_pressed_cb/canvas_clicked_cb + reset/restart/cancel_cb. Documented in docs/solutions/best-practices/lvgl-swipe-vs-tap-gesture-guard.md.

kyac (Ken's LangChain/LangGraph homelab controller, github.com/kenhia/kyac) shipped sprint 007 consolidation 2026-07-10: a fresh-eyes external review of sprints 001-006 found 3 HIGH-severity read-only-tier approval bypasses INHERITED VERBATIM FROM kagent's shell.py gate — and by extension present in any repo sharing that allowlist DNA (kagent, kmon). The holes: (1) allowlisted programs hide mutations in their argument space — `find -delete`/`-fprintf` write/delete files, `git --output=<file>` writes an arbitrary attacker-controlled file (CRITICAL, `--format=format:<literal> --output=~/.ssh/authorized_keys`), `ip route add`/`nvidia-smi -pm`/`journalctl --vacuum-*` mutate; (2) `env` and `ps eww` and `cat /proc/self/environ` dump the agent's own secrets (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, tokens) into model context → shared memory; (3) the fs secret denylist only guarded read_file, so `cat ~/.env`/`grep -r ~/.ssh`/symlinks bypassed it. Durable fix pattern: deny-by-spelling is leaky and needs an ADVERSARIAL SECOND PASS (the first fix looked right and still let git --output through) — use prefix-aware matching for abbreviations, a global --output deny for every program, and check directory args not just files. Backport tracked as kagent korg WI #312. Accepted residual: a read-only agent still reads what the operator can read via a non-secret-named parent — guardrail, not a boundary.

Homelab TLS + auth direction decided 2026-07-11 (doc: homelab-ai-plan/decisions/2026-07-11-tls-and-auth-direction.md): mesh-first with Tailscale free Personal plan (6 users/unlimited devices since Apr 2026). TLS = MagicDNS + `tailscale serve` with auto-renewed publicly-trusted Let's Encrypt certs on <host>.<tailnet>.ts.net — no private CA, no trust-store distribution to iPhone/browsers/CLI. Auth = tailnet identity: services bind 127.0.0.1 with tailscale serve as sole ingress, and read the injected Tailscale-User-Login / Tailscale-User-Name headers; kyac's contract is a FastAPI `current_identity` dependency returning Identity{user, display, via} with 401 on missing header, plus a KYAC_AUTH=dev localhost mode. klams keeps its bearer tokens as defense-in-depth. Rejected: proxy-first (step-ca+Caddy+Authelia+internal DNS — recurring private-root trust distribution, 4 new critical-path services), homegrown kauth, headscale (loses ts.net certs). Rollout: tailnet+iPhone first, then klams :7777 behind serve as first TLS consumer, then kvllm/korg, then kyac as first auth consumer, then close all 0.0.0.0 LAN listeners. Verified greenfield on 2026-07-11: no tailscale/proxy/auth product on kai/kubs0/kubsdb/ksandbox; LAN DNS is router 192.168.1.1 under `localdomain`; the old hand-rolled localCA from the pre-rebuild system is gone (backup path absent) and superseded.

Refinement (2026-07-11) to the homelab TLS+auth decision (doc: homelab-ai-plan/decisions/2026-07-11-tls-and-auth-direction.md): after review with Ken the plan was de-maximalized. It is now ADDITIVE and DUAL-STACK — the LAN stays up throughout, services keep their plain-HTTP LAN listener while `tailscale serve` adds an HTTPS ts.net endpoint, clients migrate one at a time, and `ssh ken@kai` over the LAN is explicitly unchanged (Tailscale is additive). The two driving goals are (1) trusted HTTPS without per-device cert-trust chores and (2) off-LAN phone access with nothing exposed. Aggressive lockdown (localhost-only binds, tailnet-only SSH) is an OPTIONAL later appendix, not a prerequisite. Device inventory: ENROLL kai, kubs0, kubsdb, ksandbox, gratch (Unraid NAS — retires the old 'replace Unraid self-signed cert' to-do; Unraid has first-class Tailscale support), the Pis, cleo (Windows), iPhone. DO NOT ENROLL kwork — it's Microsoft-managed (Ken is a Surface-team vendor); enrolling risks the corporate VPN (DNS/posture conflicts) and MDM policy rejection, and gains nothing needed. Consequence: kwork reaches korg only via LAN http (http://kubsdb:5674), leaving that one path plaintext on the LAN — accepted as no-worse-than-today (backlog data, on-LAN active interception only), with an SSH local-forward tunnel (ssh -L 5674:localhost:5674 ken@kubsdb) as the optional encryption mitigation that needs no software on the managed machine. URL change pattern: http://kubsdb:5674 -> https://kubsdb.<tailnet>.ts.net:5674 (same port; ts.net suffix required for cert validation).
